subject: Civil Engineering
title: The Three Gorges Dam
description: A quick win: understand The Three Gorges Dam.

hook.text: The world's largest hydropower station — 22,500 MW — spanning the Yangtze River in China.

buildup.text: 1.4 miles wide and 607 feet tall — it created a reservoir stretching 370 miles upstream.

discovery.text: 1.3 million people were relocated — entire cities submerged beneath the rising reservoir.

twist.text: The dam slowed Earth's rotation — shifting enough water mass to lengthen the day by 0.06 microseconds.

climax.text: It reduces downstream flooding but traps sediment — the Yangtze delta is now eroding.

punchline.text: A dam so massive it changed the planet's spin. Engineering at a scale nature notices.

quiz.question: How did the Three Gorges Dam affect Earth's rotation?
options: It blocked wind patterns that drive atmospheric rotation
Shifting massive water mass slowed Earth's rotation by 0.06 microseconds per day
Vibrations from the turbines transmitted energy into the Earth's crust

details.summary: The Three Gorges Dam on China's Yangtze River is the world's largest hydroelectric power station at 22,500 megawatts, with a concrete gravity dam 2,335 meters long and 181 meters high. Completed in 2006, it provides flood control, electricity, and navigation but displaced 1.3 million people.
details.whyItMatters: Three Gorges represents both the extraordinary capability and the enormous social and environmental cost of large dam projects, making it the most debated dam ever built.
takeaways: It generates 22,500 megawatts, making it the world's largest power station
1.3 million people were relocated from the reservoir area
The project provides flood protection for 15 million downstream residents

faq.question: What were the main arguments against building the Three Gorges Dam?
faq.answer: Critics cited displacement of 1.3 million residents, flooding of archaeological and cultural sites, destruction of river ecosystems including endangered species habitat, reservoir-induced landslide risk, sedimentation concerns, and reservoir-triggered seismicity.

faq.question: Has the Three Gorges Dam achieved its intended benefits?
faq.answer: The dam has successfully reduced major flooding on the middle and lower Yangtze, generates enormous amounts of low-carbon electricity, and improved navigation with a ship lock and ship lift.
